# 1. Overview

This notebook quantifies phylogenetic signal in host use with the Fritz & Purvis
(2010) **D-statistic** (`caper::phylo.d`), the appropriate metric for a binary
trait. It uses the same prepared inputs as the Figure 1 ancestral state
reconstruction (`../../Figure_1/code/1_host_use_ancestral_state_reconstruction.Rmd`),
so the signal test and the reconstruction rest on the same tree and host-use data:

- `../input_data/Danaini_in_HOSTS.newick` — the Danaini species tree.
- `../input_data/Ext_fig1_host_associations.csv` — the butterfly-species ×
  plant-genus associations from Extended Data Fig. 1, carrying each association's
  plant subfamily and family. Every row is a documented (present) association.

The headline test is **milkweed-clade** host use (Sections 3–5). Section 7 repeats
it for five further host groups (the non-milkweed Apocynaceae subfamilies, each on
its own, and Moraceae), all from the same association table.

```{r setup, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)

library(tidyverse)
library(ape)
library(caper)
library(ggtree)
library(ggplot2)

dir.create("../output_data", showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create("../visuals", showWarnings = FALSE)

# Canonical tip formatter: spaces -> underscores (matches the saved tree tips)
to_tip <- function(x) {
  stringr::str_replace_all(stringr::str_trim(as.character(x)), "[[:space:]]+", "_")
}

# "Danaus_plexippus" -> "D. plexippus" for plotting
abbr_tip <- function(x) {
  x <- stringr::str_squish(stringr::str_replace_all(as.character(x), "_", " "))
  vapply(x, function(z) {
    parts <- strsplit(z, " ")[[1]]
    if (length(parts) >= 2 && nchar(parts[1]) > 0)
      paste0(substr(parts[1], 1, 1), ". ", parts[2]) else z
  }, character(1))
}
```

# 2. Read and prepare the phylogeny

`caper::phylo.d` requires (i) no labels shared between tips and internal nodes and
(ii) no zero-length internal branches. We strip the bootstrap node labels and, if
any internal branch has length zero, nudge it to a tiny positive value (1e-8,
far below the smallest positive branch length) so the dichotomous topology is
preserved rather than collapsed to a polytomy.

```{r read-tree}
tree0 <- ape::read.tree("../input_data/Danaini_in_HOSTS.newick")
tree0$tip.label <- to_tip(tree0$tip.label)

# (i) remove support labels shared with tips
tree0$node.label <- NULL

# (ii) nudge any zero-length internal branches (topology preserved)
n_zero <- sum(tree0$edge.length == 0)
tree0$edge.length[tree0$edge.length == 0] <- 1e-8

# (iii) orient the tree to the curated reference order (shared with Extended Data
# Fig. 1 / Figure 2 and the ASR notebook) so the trait-on-tree figures match that
# orientation. Rotation changes only the display, not the D-statistic (which is
# order-independent) or the topology. Heliconius erato is absent from the reference
# tree, so it is placed at the base with the other outgroups.
reference_tree <- ape::read.tree("../input_data/danaini_reference_order.newick")
reference_tree$tip.label <- to_tip(reference_tree$tip.label)
reference_order <- {
  d <- ggtree(reference_tree, ladderize = FALSE)$data
  d <- d[d$isTip, ]
  to_tip(d$label[order(d$y, decreasing = TRUE)])
}
reference_order <- c(reference_order, "Heliconius_erato")
tree0 <- ape::rotateConstr(tree0, rev(intersect(reference_order, tree0$tip.label)))

cat("Tree tips:", length(tree0$tip.label),
    "| rooted:", ape::is.rooted(tree0),
    "| dichotomous:", ape::is.binary(tree0),
    "| zero-length branches nudged:", n_zero, "\n")
```

# 3. Build the binary milkweed-clade trait

```{r read-assoc}
milkweed_subfams <- c("Asclepiadoideae", "Secamonoideae")

assoc <- read.csv(
  "../input_data/Ext_fig1_host_associations.csv",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) %>%
  mutate(butterfly_species = to_tip(butterfly_species))
```

```{r build-trait}
# milkweed = 1 if the species has >= 1 association in the milkweed clade.
trait_df <- assoc %>%
  group_by(butterfly_species) %>%
  summarise(milkweed = as.integer(any(plant_subfamily %in% milkweed_subfams)),
            .groups = "drop")

# Every tree tip needs a value; tips absent from the association table are coded 0.
trait_full <- tibble(butterfly_species = tree0$tip.label) %>%
  left_join(trait_df, by = "butterfly_species") %>%
  mutate(milkweed = tidyr::replace_na(milkweed, 0L)) %>%
  as.data.frame()

cat("Trait distribution (milkweed use):\n"); print(table(trait_full$milkweed))
cat("Tree tips absent from the association table (coded 0):\n")
print(setdiff(tree0$tip.label, trait_df$butterfly_species))
```

# 4. Fritz & Purvis D-statistic

```{r phylo-d}
set.seed(1)  # phylo.d permutes/simulates; fix the seed for reproducibility

fit_d <- caper::phylo.d(
  data = trait_full, phy = tree0,
  names.col = butterfly_species, binvar = milkweed, permut = 1000
)
fit_d

sink("../output_data/fritz_purvis_D_milkweed_phylo_signal.txt")
print(fit_d)
sink()
```

**Interpretation.** The D-statistic measures how a binary trait is distributed
across a phylogeny relative to two reference models: **D ≈ 0** = as clumped as a
Brownian threshold model (phylogenetically conserved); **D ≈ 1** = random with
respect to the phylogeny; **D < 0** = more clumped than Brownian; **D > 1** =
overdispersed. **P(D = 1)** tests departure from random (small = significant
signal); **P(D = 0)** tests departure from the Brownian expectation.

# 5. Visualization

## 5.1 D relative to the random and Brownian null distributions

```{r fig-nulldist, fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
d_obs <- unname(fit_d$DEstimate)

# caper stores permutation values on the raw sum-of-changes scale; rescale linearly
# so Brownian ~ 0 and random ~ 1 (the interpretable D axis).
mean_brown <- mean(fit_d$Permutations$brownian)
mean_rand  <- mean(fit_d$Permutations$random)
to_D <- function(x) (x - mean_brown) / (mean_rand - mean_brown)

null_df <- bind_rows(
  tibble(D = to_D(as.numeric(fit_d$Permutations$random)),   model = "Random (no signal)"),
  tibble(D = to_D(as.numeric(fit_d$Permutations$brownian)), model = "Brownian (conserved)")
) %>%
  mutate(model = factor(model, levels = c("Brownian (conserved)", "Random (no signal)")))

null_palette <- c("Brownian (conserved)" = "#65338f", "Random (no signal)" = "grey65")

# The observed D and its p-values are exported to the summary table (Section 7.7),
# not drawn on the figure; the vertical line marks the observed D on the plot.
p_null <- ggplot(null_df, aes(D, fill = model, colour = model)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.45, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = d_obs, linewidth = 0.8, colour = "black") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = null_palette, name = NULL) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = null_palette, name = NULL) +
  labs(title = "Phylogenetic signal in milkweed-clade host use (Fritz & Purvis D)",
       x = "D statistic", y = "Density") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "right")

p_null
ggsave("../visuals/hostplant_phylo_signal_D_nulldist.png",
       p_null, width = 8, height = 5, dpi = 300)
```

## 5.2 Milkweed-clade use mapped on the phylogeny

```{r fig-trait-tree, fig.width=9, fig.height=11}
trait_strip <- data.frame(
  milkweed = factor(ifelse(trait_full$milkweed == 1L, "milkweed", "none"),
                    levels = c("none", "milkweed")),
  row.names = trait_full$butterfly_species
)
trait_strip <- trait_strip[tree0$tip.label, , drop = FALSE]

pt <- ggtree(tree0, branch.length = "none", ladderize = FALSE,
             size = 0.3, color = "grey40")
tree_xmax <- max(pt$data$x, na.rm = TRUE)

pt <- gheatmap(pt, trait_strip, offset = 0.01, width = 0.04,
               colnames = FALSE, color = NA) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    name   = "Milkweed-clade use",
    values = c("milkweed" = "#65338f", "none" = "grey90"),
    breaks = c("milkweed", "none"),
    labels = c("Asclepiadoideae & Secamonoideae", "Non-milkweed"),
    drop   = FALSE
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = c(0.08, 0.92), legend.justification = c(0, 1),
        legend.background = element_blank(), legend.key.size = unit(0.35, "cm"))

pt <- pt +
  geom_tiplab(aes(label = abbr_tip(label)), offset = tree_xmax * 0.10,
              size = 2.4, fontface = "italic", align = TRUE, linetype = 0) +
  xlim_tree(tree_xmax + 9)

pt
ggsave("../visuals/hostplant_phylo_signal_trait_tree.png",
       pt, width = 9, height = 11, dpi = 300)
```

# 6. Justification for the trait coding

- **The trait is binary, not continuous.** Host use is presence/absence of an
  association with a host group, a discrete state. Fritz & Purvis's D was
  developed for binary traits (evaluated against random and Brownian threshold
  expectations); Pagel's λ, by contrast, is for continuously distributed traits
  and is not appropriate here.

- **Source consistency with the reconstruction.** The trait is built from the same
  Extended Data Fig. 1 association table that underlies the ancestral state
  reconstruction, so the two analyses are directly comparable. Because that table
  applies Figure 1's native-range *Asclepias* rule, a species whose only milkweed
  record is a non-native *Asclepias* association is coded `0` here, matching the
  reconstruction.

- **Presence threshold (≥ 1 record).** A documented association is treated as
  evidence of use: a species is coded `1` for a host group if it has at least one
  recorded association in that group.

- **Definition of the milkweed clade.** The subfamilies **Asclepiadoideae** and
  **Secamonoideae**, the monophyletic milkweed lineage within Apocynaceae.

- **The `0` state.** A species is coded `0` for a host group when it has documented
  host use outside that group, or when it is absent from the association table
  (the outgroups and any ingroup tip with no Apocynaceae/Moraceae association). All
  tree tips are retained.

# 7. Phylogenetic signal for additional host groups

The milkweed-clade analysis (Sections 3–5) is repeated verbatim — same tree, same
≥ 1-record presence coding, same `caper::phylo.d` call and the same two figures —
for five further host groups: the non-milkweed Apocynaceae subfamilies combined,
each of them alone (Periplocoideae, Apocynoideae, Rauvolfioideae), and Moraceae.

## 7.1 Reusable helper

```{r group-signal-helper}
# Linear rescaling of caper's raw permutation values onto the D axis (Section 5.1).
rescale_to_D <- function(fit) {
  mean_brown <- mean(fit$Permutations$brownian)
  mean_rand  <- mean(fit$Permutations$random)
  function(x) (x - mean_brown) / (mean_rand - mean_brown)
}

# predicate: function of the association data frame returning a logical vector
#            (TRUE = the row counts as use of this host group).
# slug:      filename stem; title: plot title; use_label: legend label for "use".
run_group_signal <- function(predicate, slug, title, use_label,
                             fig_nulldist = TRUE, fig_tree = TRUE) {
  assoc_use <- assoc
  assoc_use$.use <- as.logical(predicate(assoc))
  trait_df <- assoc_use %>%
    group_by(butterfly_species) %>%
    summarise(trait = as.integer(any(.use)), .groups = "drop")

  trait_full <- tibble(butterfly_species = tree0$tip.label) %>%
    left_join(trait_df, by = "butterfly_species") %>%
    mutate(trait = tidyr::replace_na(trait, 0L)) %>%
    as.data.frame()

  cat("## ", title, "\n", sep = "")
  cat("Trait distribution (", slug, "):\n", sep = ""); print(table(trait_full$trait))

  set.seed(1)
  fit <- caper::phylo.d(
    data = trait_full, phy = tree0,
    names.col = butterfly_species, binvar = trait, permut = 1000
  )
  print(fit)

  sink(sprintf("../output_data/fritz_purvis_D_%s_phylo_signal.txt", slug))
  cat(title, "\n\n"); print(fit)
  sink()

  if (fig_nulldist) {
    d_obs <- unname(fit$DEstimate)
    to_D  <- rescale_to_D(fit)
    null_df <- bind_rows(
      tibble(D = to_D(as.numeric(fit$Permutations$random)),   model = "Random (no signal)"),
      tibble(D = to_D(as.numeric(fit$Permutations$brownian)), model = "Brownian (conserved)")
    ) %>%
      mutate(model = factor(model, levels = c("Brownian (conserved)", "Random (no signal)")))

    # D and p-values go to the summary table (Section 7.7), not onto the figure.
    p_null <- ggplot(null_df, aes(D, fill = model, colour = model)) +
      geom_density(alpha = 0.45, linewidth = 0.3) +
      geom_vline(xintercept = d_obs, linewidth = 0.8, colour = "black") +
      scale_fill_manual(values = c("Brownian (conserved)" = "#65338f",
                                   "Random (no signal)" = "grey65"), name = NULL) +
      scale_colour_manual(values = c("Brownian (conserved)" = "#65338f",
                                     "Random (no signal)" = "grey65"), name = NULL) +
      labs(title = sprintf("Phylogenetic signal in %s (Fritz & Purvis D)", title),
           x = "D statistic", y = "Density") +
      theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
      theme(legend.position = "right")

    print(p_null)
    ggsave(sprintf("../visuals/hostplant_phylo_signal_D_nulldist_%s.png", slug),
           p_null, width = 8, height = 5, dpi = 300)
  }

  if (fig_tree) {
    trait_strip <- data.frame(
      use = factor(ifelse(trait_full$trait == 1L, "use", "none"),
                   levels = c("none", "use")),
      row.names = trait_full$butterfly_species
    )
    trait_strip <- trait_strip[tree0$tip.label, , drop = FALSE]

    pt <- ggtree(tree0, branch.length = "none", ladderize = FALSE,
                 size = 0.3, color = "grey40")
    tree_xmax <- max(pt$data$x, na.rm = TRUE)

    pt <- gheatmap(pt, trait_strip, offset = 0.01, width = 0.04,
                   colnames = FALSE, color = NA) +
      scale_fill_manual(name = "Host use",
                        values = c("use" = "#65338f", "none" = "grey90"),
                        breaks = c("use", "none"),
                        labels = c(use_label, "No association"), drop = FALSE) +
      theme(legend.position = c(0.08, 0.92), legend.justification = c(0, 1),
            legend.background = element_blank(), legend.key.size = unit(0.35, "cm"))

    pt <- pt +
      geom_tiplab(aes(label = abbr_tip(label)), offset = tree_xmax * 0.10,
                  size = 2.4, fontface = "italic", align = TRUE, linetype = 0) +
      xlim_tree(tree_xmax + 9)

    print(pt)
    ggsave(sprintf("../visuals/hostplant_phylo_signal_trait_tree_%s.png", slug),
           pt, width = 9, height = 11, dpi = 300)
  }

  invisible(fit)
}
```

## 7.2 Non-milkweed Apocynaceae (Periplocoideae + Apocynoideae + Rauvolfioideae)

```{r signal-nonmilkweed-apocynaceae, fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
nonmilkweed_subfams <- c("Periplocoideae", "Apocynoideae", "Rauvolfioideae")
fit_nonmilkweed <- run_group_signal(
  predicate = function(df) df$plant_subfamily %in% nonmilkweed_subfams,
  slug      = "nonmilkweed_apocynaceae",
  title     = "non-milkweed Apocynaceae (Periploc.+Apocyn.+Rauvolf.) host use",
  use_label = "Periplocoideae, Apocynoideae & Rauvolfioideae"
)
```

## 7.7 Summary of D across host groups

```{r signal-summary}
signal_summary <- tibble::tribble(
  ~host_group,                                              ~fit,
  "Milkweed clade (Asclepiadoideae & Secamonoideae)",       list(fit_d),
  "Non-milkweed Apocynaceae (Periploc.+Apocyn.+Rauvolf.)",  list(fit_nonmilkweed),
  "Periplocoideae",                                         list(fit_periplocoideae),
  "Apocynoideae",                                           list(fit_apocynoideae),
  "Rauvolfioideae",                                         list(fit_rauvolfioideae),
  "Moraceae",                                               list(fit_moraceae)
) %>%
  mutate(
    D         = vapply(fit, function(f) unname(f[[1]]$DEstimate), numeric(1)),
    `P(D=1)`  = vapply(fit, function(f) f[[1]]$Pval1, numeric(1)),
    `P(D=0)`  = vapply(fit, function(f) f[[1]]$Pval0, numeric(1)),
    n_present = vapply(fit, function(f) as.integer(f[[1]]$StatesTable["1"]), integer(1))
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(-fit) %>%
  # Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction across the six host groups, applied within
  # each p-value family separately. P(D=1) tests for phylogenetic signal (departure
  # from a random distribution) and is the test of interest; P(D=0) tests departure
  # from the Brownian expectation. A permutation p-value of 0 means < 1/1000.
  mutate(
    `P(D=1)_BH` = p.adjust(`P(D=1)`, method = "BH"),
    `P(D=0)_BH` = p.adjust(`P(D=0)`, method = "BH")
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(host_group, n_present, D,
                `P(D=1)`, `P(D=1)_BH`, `P(D=0)`, `P(D=0)_BH`)

knitr::kable(signal_summary, digits = 3,
             caption = paste("Fritz & Purvis D-statistic across host groups,",
                             "with Benjamini-Hochberg (FDR) corrected p-values"))

# All numeric results (D, raw and BH-corrected p-values, n) live in this table, so
# the figures carry no on-plot statistics; add them when assembling the panel.
write.csv(signal_summary,
          "../output_data/fritz_purvis_D_host_group_summary.csv",
          row.names = FALSE)
```
